label: Group Actions on Symplectic Manifolds
notes: Open by framing Lecture 21 as the grammar lesson before moment maps. We move from a single complete vector field to whole Lie groups acting smoothly, then sharpen the action so each element is a symplectomorphism. Stress that everything here is preparation for asking when an action is Hamiltonian.

label: One-Parameter Groups and Flows
notes: Explain that a complete vector field integrates to a flow indexed by real time. The group law is not a new axiom; it follows because composing flows and flowing directly solve the same initial value problem, so uniqueness of integral curves forces them to agree. This is the seed of every action.

label: Lie Groups and Smooth Actions
notes: Define a Lie group as a manifold whose multiplication and inversion are smooth, and a smooth action as a homomorphism into diffeomorphisms with smooth evaluation. Emphasize the associativity and identity axioms, and that small matrix groups like rotations and unitaries are our reliable working models throughout the lecture.

label: Orbits and Stabilizers
notes: Introduce the orbit as the reachable set and the stabilizer as the subgroup fixing a point. The orbit-stabilizer correspondence controls local shape. Walk through translation lines, rotation circles, and the sphere with two fixed poles, and note that these dimensions foreshadow why quotient spaces need free and proper hypotheses.

label: Free, Proper, Effective
notes: Carefully separate the three adjectives. Effective means only the identity acts trivially everywhere; free means no nontrivial element fixes any point; proper controls escape to infinity so quotients stay Hausdorff manifolds. Stress that free plus proper is the standard package guaranteeing the orbit space is a smooth manifold.

label: Symplectic Actions
notes: Define a symplectic action: every group element pulls the form back to itself, acting through symplectomorphisms. For a linear action on standard space this is exactly the matrix identity A transpose J A equals J. Demonstrate with a rotation; the residual vanishes, so rotations of the plane are genuinely symplectic.

label: The Infinitesimal Action
notes: Differentiate a one-parameter subgroup to get the generating vector field X-sharp at each point. This is the bridge from the Lie algebra to vector fields on the manifold: each algebra element produces a flow whose velocity is X-sharp, tangent to the orbit. The map is a Lie algebra anti-homomorphism into vector fields.

label: Generating Vector Field on an Orbit
notes: Use the orbit picture to make X-sharp tangible. Trace a one-parameter subgroup through a point and draw its velocity arrow tangent to the orbit curve. Emphasize that X-sharp vanishes exactly where the stabilizer is positive dimensional, linking the infinitesimal picture back to fixed points and poles.

label: Cotangent Lift: Always Symplectic
notes: Show that any action on a base manifold lifts to its cotangent bundle and that lift automatically preserves the tautological one-form, hence the canonical symplectic form. This is the workhorse example: every smooth group action on configuration space gives a symplectic, indeed Hamiltonian, action on phase space.

label: Rotation Action on R^2 = C
notes: Work the rotation of the plane in detail. The generator X-sharp is the rotational field minus y, x, and contracting the area form with it gives the differential of minus one half r squared. So the circle action is not just symplectic but Hamiltonian, with that radial function as Hamiltonian. Preview torus actions as products of such circles.

label: Prelude to Moment Maps
notes: Close by separating two properties: preserving omega is a property of the action, while having a Hamiltonian for each generator is an extra exactness condition. Adjoint and coadjoint representations supply the equivariance bookkeeping. Lecture 22 will assemble one Hamiltonian per algebra direction into a single moment map landing in the dual Lie algebra.
